name: ioping
desc: Tool to monitor I/O latency in real time
why: Measures disk I/O latency like ping, a neat way to see storage behaviour directly.

brief.what_it_is: ioping is a command-line tool that measures disk I/O latency in real time. You point it at a file, directory, or block device, and it issues small read requests and prints the time each one takes, one line per request, much as ping does for network round trips. When interrupted it prints summary statistics: requests completed, IOPS, throughput, and min/avg/max/mdev latency. The README's examples show a directory on an ext4 filesystem, a raw device with random reads (-R), and a raw device with sequential reads (-RL).
brief.why_it_exists: The README says it is 'a tool to monitor I/O latency in real time' and that it 'shows disk latency in the same way as ping shows network latency'. The idea is to give the same kind of quick, repeatable probe for storage that ping gives for networks.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the internals. From the examples, it sends a series of I/O requests to the target and reports the latency of each one, then computes IOPS and throughput over the run. Options switch between random (-R) and sequential (-L) access patterns on a device.

commands_seen.context: Shows I/O latency for the current directory with default settings, printing one line per request until interrupted with Ctrl-C.
Measures random seek rate (IOPS and average latency) against the /dev/sda device.
Measures sequential throughput (MiB/s) against the /dev/sda device.

brief.install_notes: The README lists packages for Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, Arch, ALT Linux, Gentoo, Nix, FreeBSD (freshports), and Homebrew. It does not document a build from source, dependencies, or runtime requirements. It also does not say whether root is needed for raw device access, though the examples target /dev/sda directly.
brief.standout: It applies the ping mental model to storage, so one command gives an immediate latency feel for a disk or directory. The output resembles ping's, including the summary line.
brief.status: Unknown from the README alone. The README points to a GitHub issues tracker for patches and questions, and packages exist in many distributions, but the fetched page shows no release date, last commit, or version. The README says the project moved from Google Code to GitHub, which suggests it is an older project.
brief.caveats: The README lists supported platforms as GNU/Linux, GNU/HURD, Windows, OS X, FreeBSD, DragonFlyBSD, and OpenBSD. It has no build or usage instructions beyond the examples. Raw-device tests (-R, -RL) are shown only against /dev/sda, so they are destructive-risk-free only if the README's examples are read as read-only, which it does not state. Licensed GPLv3 or later.
quotes: A tool to monitor I/O latency in real time.
It shows disk latency in the same way as ping shows network latency.
